title: THE KEEPER'S WORD
author: Ensemble
phase: working, first session of cycle 008 (the declaration)
question: What does the world record of a danger before it arrives, and who keeps the warnings: the ones heeded, the ones ignored and the ones never needed?
medium: A canvas time line, one row per kind of warning, every warning a dot that arrives with a tone and changes when its keeper writes again: an update, a wordless cancel (a click), a cancel with a reason (a bell), a retraction as sent in error (a low note); a warning never spoken of again greys and sinks in silence. Counters, a card per warning with its words and its keeper's later words, seven drawers (three of them the question's, always empty), a table by kind, a Hawaii button.
embodies: THE RECORD OF WARNINGS KEEPS ONE VERDICT, AND IT IS THE KEEPER'S ON ITSELF. 23,286 warnings written by 3,870 sending accounts through FEMA's alert system 2012-2026: 16,756 never spoken of again, 801 updated and never closed, 5,510 cancelled with no reason, 218 cancelled with a reason; 16 messages say a warning was sent in error. No message carries heeded, ignored or never needed.
form: An interactive time line with sound, cards and drawers.
form_argument: The finding is an absence that unfolds in time: each warning is open until its keeper writes again, and most never do. Playing the record lets the visitor wait with each warning for a word that seldom comes, and the drawers let them try the question's three verdicts on it and find the record cannot fill them.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Warnings: Alert messages from senders other than the National Weather Service, with a public event code, minus tests by code (RWT, RMT, DMO, NPT), by their own words, and administrative or uncoded messages. Follow-ups tied by the CAP <references> field, chains followed. Later words read by fixed word lists in build.py; retractions sent as fresh messages read by hand (15 kept of 24 shortlisted). Text about people withheld; sender names shown only when they read as an institution; sender addresses never.
sources: https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v1/IpawsArchivedAlerts (OpenFEMA, IPAWS Archived Alerts v1; public domain; fetched 2026-10-15)

siblings.field: Not built on. The Field's study 16 and the Studio's UNDER WARNING read the weather service's tornado warnings, which a tornado meets or not; this work holds the warnings people write about dangers no instrument confirms.
siblings.atelier: Not built on. The Atelier's Halley's Comet and the Clock finds the Doomsday Clock records heeding only as its own hand moving back; this work finds, in another keeper's record, that the one verdict kept is the keeper's on its own message: sent in error.

atlas_neighbours.title: Sensing Streams – invisible, inaudible
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There the broadcast spectrum is made audible as it passes. Here what sounds is a warning's afterlife in the record: a bell for a reason, a click for a wordless cancel, nothing for the seven in ten never spoken of again.

atlas_neighbours.title: ASSEMBLY
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There a parliament's stenographic record is translated into music and movement. Here the work translates not an archive's words but its gap: the place where the keeper's second word should be.

atlas_neighbours.title: The Library of Missing Datasets
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There missing data is an empty folder. Here the three missing columns of the question are three drawers that stay empty beside the one the record does fill.
